definitions.explanation: A luminous point in the night sky.

examples.japanese: {空|そら}に{星|ほし}がたくさん{見|み}える。
examples.english: Many stars are visible in the sky.

examples.japanese: {山|やま}の{上|うえ}から{見|み}る{星|ほし}はとてもきれいだ。
examples.english: The stars seen from the mountaintop are very beautiful.

examples.japanese: {夏|なつ}の{夜|よる}に{父|ちち}と{外|そと}に{出|で}て、{一緒|いっしょ}に{星|ほし}を{見|み}るのが{楽|たの}しい。
examples.english: On summer nights, it's fun to go outside with my father and look at the stars together.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}の{時|とき}、{毎年|まいとし}{夏|なつ}になると{父|ちち}と{山|やま}に{行|い}って、{一緒|いっしょ}に{星|ほし}を{見|み}るのが{楽|たの}しかった。
examples.english: When I was a child, every summer I would go to the mountains with my father, and it was fun to look at the stars together.

notes:
{星|ほし} refers primarily to stars visible in the night sky, not planets in scientific contexts.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {星|ほし}を{見|み}る: to look at stars
- {星|ほし}が{出|で}る: stars come out
- {星|ほし}が{輝|かがや}く: stars shine
- {流|なが}れ{星|ぼし}: shooting star
- {星空|ほしぞら}: starry sky

COMPOUNDS:
- {星座|せいざ}: constellation
- {一番星|いちばんぼし}: first star of evening
- {北極星|ほっきょくせい}: North Star

FIGURATIVE USE:
{星|ほし} also means rating stars ({三|み}つ{星|ぼし} = three stars) and can refer to someone's destiny or fate in literary contexts.

SCIENCE NOTE:
In astronomy, {恒星|こうせい} (fixed star) is the technical term, while {惑星|わくせい} refers to planets.
